diagnoses.description: Date disambiguation failure: the original run selected a secondary date-like token (likely from an OCR-corrupted label line such as DATE→DATA) instead of the primary header Date field. This is consistent with a first-match regex strategy without header/label ranking.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 034.jpg date_correct=false while amount_correct=true; prediction date=2018-08-09. Source-run OCR snippets show a competing header-adjacent line like “Salesperson. Data: 09/08/2018”, while the image shows a clear header “Date: 09/03/2018”. The source implementation (per atif_steps references) used first-match date extraction without label/context ranking, making this failure mode likely.

diagnoses.description: Total selection failure driven by OCR digit-flip outlier (102.00→702.00) on a TOTAL-like line and a selection rule that prefers the last TOTAL candidate. Without an anchor-consistency override (Subtotal/Payment agreement) and/or an upscale OCR pass, the outlier can dominate.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 074.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount=702.00. OCR snippets show anchors “Subtotal : 102.00” and “Payment : 102.00” but also a corrupted “Total ... 702.00”. The run’s own debugging shows that 2× upscaling + autocontrast + PSM6 yields clean “Total incl. of GST 102.00”, indicating OCR configuration plus anchor-consistency are decisive.

diagnoses.description: Rounding precedence failure: the run selected the pre-rounding inclusive total instead of the final payable TOTAL after a rounding adjustment. This requires an unconditional precedence rule to avoid exact-match misses.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 077.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount=23.26. The image shows “Rounding Adj: -0.01” followed by bold “TOTAL: 23.25”, while an earlier line shows “Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26”. The miss is selection/precedence, not OCR absence.

diagnoses.description: Schema/normalization failure: total_amount was emitted as an empty string instead of null. Additionally, this receipt layout includes an AMOUNT column header that can trigger split-line fallback to an item amount unless explicitly excluded; OCR may also corrupt the GRAND TOTAL keyword and decimal separator (e.g., 92:80).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 078.jpg amount_correct=false; prediction total_amount="" violates task requirement (must be null on failure). Source-run trace shows matching on “Description Qty Price Amount” and split-line fallback to an item amount; other OCR variants show “GrandTota.” and “92:80”. Even when extraction fails, output must be null, never empty string.

quality_impact.rationale: No changes proposed because the current candidate image-ocr skill already documents the missing behaviors evidenced in the source run: header/label-tolerant date ranking, rounding precedence, anchor-consistency override, header-line exclusion, decimal-separator normalization, and an explicit empty-string→null guard. The historical failures are primarily due to the original implementation not applying these rules (first-match date; last-match total; weak fallback gating), rather than missing skill guidance.

trigger_precision.rationale: By not broadening or altering skill triggers further, we avoid over-broad heuristics that could regress correct cases. The candidate’s existing rules are already tightly gated (e.g., split-line fallback only when keyword line has no digits and is not a header; anchor override only when multiple anchors agree; optional upscaling only as fallback).

skillaxe_evaluation.overall_rationale: The packet’s evidence indicates the original run’s misses were dominated by receipt-specific selection/normalization under OCR noise, not missing OCR capability. The current candidate image-ocr SKILL.md already encodes minimal, transferable heuristics to address these failures. Therefore, this iteration recommends no further SKILL.md changes; the next improvement would be ensuring downstream implementations actually apply the documented rules (especially: header-date preference, anchor-consistency override, rounding precedence, header-line exclusion, and final schema guard).
